title: Petrol,diesel prices reduced
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has announced a reduction in the prices of selected fuel types with effect from last night (29).

title: Paraguay Stun Germany on Penalties in One of the Greatest FIFA World Cup Upsets
byline: Germany’s FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign came to a stunning end as Paraguay pulled off one of the greatest upsets in tournament history, defeating the four-time champions 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in their Round of 32 clash.

title: Water plant turns out to be illegal liquor factory; 18,575 bottles seized
byline: A large-scale illegal liquor manufacturing operation disguised as a bottled drinking water business has been busted in Kaduwela, with police seizing more than 18,500 bottles of illicit liquor and arresting six suspects during a raid.

title: Oil stocks in US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fall by 5.5 million to lowest level since 1983
byline: Stocks of ​crude oil in the U.S. ‌Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by 5.5 million barrels to 325.7 million barrels, ​the lowest level since May ​1983, according to data from the ⁠Department of Energy.

title: Two drown after boat capsizes in Loggal Oya
byline: A double canoe raft conveying a group of individuals on a picnic capsized in the Loggal Oya, and two of them drowned. The bodies were recovered last morning by Hasalaka Life Guard Unit and the Maduru Oya STF with the help of the Hasalaka Police.

title: CoPF member wants Central Bank, 13 commercial banks to be held to account
byline: New Democratic Front (NDF) MP who is a member of Committee on Finance (COPF) Ravi Karunanayake in a letter addressed to the Chairman of COPF Harsha de Silva urged him to hold the Central Bank Supervision Unit and its Financial Investigation Unit answerable for what he called lethargic and oversight blindness of the institution with regard to the billion dollar illegal transfer of funds which was revealed by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake

title: Enhanced rains no cause for alarm: Met. Dept.
byline: Though it was reported yesterday that rains have enhanced in some parts of the country, including the catchment areas, the Department of Meteorology yesterday ruled out disaster in the coming days.

title: US and Iran negotiators head to Doha, but meeting uncertain
byline: Iranian and U.S. negotiating ​teams were due in Doha this week, but Iran said on Monday no meeting had been scheduled as weekend missile fire from both sides tested the interim ceasefire ‌to end the four-month-old war.

title: Sri Lanka woos U.S. investments for Colombo Port development
byline: Sri Lanka has wooed U.S. investment in the development of the Colombo port and integrated infrastructure at a recent summit in Washington, a Deputy Minister said yesterday.

title: Six people shot dead at centre for mothers and children in Germany
byline: Six people have been fatally shot at a centre for mothers and children by a suspect who was in a custody dispute over his baby daughter, German police say.

title: Asset declaration deadline ends today; CIABOC warns of legal action
byline: The deadline for public officials and other individuals required by law to submit their annual declarations of assets and liabilities without incurring penalties expires today (30), the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) said.

title: Chinese tycoon sentenced to 30 years in US jail
byline: Guo Wengui, who was once believed to be one of China’s richest businessmen, has been sentenced to 30 years in jail in the US for running a billion dollar scam.

title: WhatsApp now lets you reserve usernames
byline: WhatsApp announced a much-awaited feature: usernames, which will allow users to share their profiles without disclosing their phone number. However, WhatsApp will still require a phone number to create an account on the chat app.

title: NDB fraud probe reveals bigger transaction trail than first disclosed
byline: Nearly three months after National Development Bank (NDB) disclosed what became one of the largest fraud cases to hit a listed Sri Lankan bank, a forensic review has identified the suspicious transaction amount to be higher than what was initially disclosed.

title: Rs.100bn revenue leakage looms for motor industry, warns CMTA
byline: Sri Lanka’s automotive industry could see government revenue leakages exceed Rs.100 billion by the end of this year, due to unchecked regulatory loopholes and systemic undervaluation, Ceylon Motor Traders Association (CMTA) Chairman Andrew Perera warned.

title: Auto industry not a cash cow for revenue collection, Chamber warns
byline: The government must stop treating the automotive industry as a reactionary tool to hit short-term fiscal targets and instead recognise it as a core driver of national industrial development, Ceylon Chamber of Commerce Secretary General and CEO Shiran Fernando said.

title: Bribery Commission issues notice on asset and liability declarations
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has announced an extension of the deadline for submitting annual and post-retirement asset and liability declarations without a penalty, following severe congestion on its centralized electronic system.

title: Rs. 80,000 bill puts Aluthgama station in the dark
byline: The electricity supply to Aluthgama Railway Station is set to be disconnected after the station reportedly failed to settle an outstanding electricity bill of nearly Rs. 80,000.

title: IMF concludes visit to Sri Lanka
byline: The International Monetary Fund staff have concluded their visit to Sri Lanka, the head of the IMF’s Sri Lanka mission Evan Papageorgiou said on Tuesday.

title: Updated World Test Championship standings after West Indies’ record win over Sri Lanka
byline: Amir Jangoo’s stunning double century, Roston Chase’s 194 and Kemar Roach’s second-innings four-fer, which took him to 300 Test wickets, helped the home side in North Sound win the first of the two-match series. This was the West Indies’ first victory after going winless in eight Tests since beating Pakistan in January last year.

title: Penalty Shockwave at World Cup: Germany fall, Morocco stun Netherlands, Iran exit triggers US Political reaction
byline: A high-stakes day at the FIFA World Cup 2026 saw shock eliminations, late winners, and political controversy as knockout football delivered major talking points across multiple continents.

title: Mr. Kottu restaurant chain owner released on bail
byline: The owner of a popular kottu restaurant chain in Sri Lanka, who was arrested over the alleged assault of an employee, was today (30) released on bail by the Nugegoda Magistrate’s Court.

title: Private sector labour shortage forces industries to recruit foreign workers: Minister
byline: Minister of Industries and Entrepreneurship Development Sunil Handunnetti has said that the private sector currently has more than 400,000 job vacancies, forcing local industries to recruit foreign workers due to a shortage of both skilled and unskilled labour.

title: Russia says it downed 419 Ukrainian drones overnight
byline: Russia’s Defense Ministry said on Tuesday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed 419 Ukrainian drones overnight, including several that were heading toward Moscow.

title: No reduction in school transport, three-wheeler fares
byline: Associations representing school transport service providers and three-wheeler operators have stated that they will not be able to reduce school transportation charges and three-wheeler rental fees despite the recent reduction in fuel prices.

title: Lal Kantha blocks camera while dodging questions on paddy procurement
byline: Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation, K.D. Lal Kantha, drew criticism after abruptly halting a media interaction and physically blocking a camera lens to avoid further questioning regarding the ongoing Yala season paddy procurement crisis.

title: Founder of Asian super-app Gojek sentenced to years in jail for corruption
byline: The co-founder of super-app Gojek who became Indonesia’s education minister has been sentenced to several years in jail for corruption.

title: Pillayan remanded over Eastern Province murders
byline: Former State Minister Sivanesathurai Chandrakanthan, alias ’’Pillayan’’, has been remanded until July 13 in connection with ongoing investigations into five murders that took place in several parts of the Eastern Province in 2008.

title: Former National Lotteries Board Chairperson Shyamila Perera arrested
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has arrested Shyamila Perera, the former Chairperson of the National Lotteries Board (NLB), a short while ago.

title: Suspect arrested with five unregistered high-capacity motorbikes
byline: A 25-year-old suspect has been arrested for possessing five unregistered high-capacity motorbikes during a raid carried out by officers of the Homagama Divisional Crime Investigation Unit.

title: Navy Commander Kanchana Banagoda promoted to Admiral ahead of retirement
byline: The Commander of the Sri Lanka Navy, Vice Admiral Kanchana Banagoda, has been promoted to the rank of Admiral.

title: Sniper rifle and ammunition recovered in Damana Forest Reserve
byline: A sniper rifle and ammunition have been recovered during a special operation conducted by officers attached to the Thirukkovil Police Special Task Force (STF) camp.

title: Sajith Premadasa urges science-based national preparedness for emerging climate risks
byline: Leader of the Opposition Sajith Premadasa today called for Sri Lanka to adopt a whole-of-government, science-based approach to climate resilience and disaster preparedness, emphasising that climate security has become a national priority that transcends political differences.

title: Mr. Kottu restaurant chain owner arrested over alleged assault of employee
byline: The owner of the popular ’’Mr. Kottu’’ restaurant chain, Viraj Wickramanayake, has been arrested in connection with the alleged assault of one of his employees.

title: Guaranteed paddy prices announced for 2026 Yala season
byline: The Government has announced the guaranteed prices at which it will purchase paddy from farmers during the 2026 Yala cultivation season

title: BOI gets new chairman and members
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed Presidential Senior Economic Adviser Duminda Hulangamuwa as the new Chairman and a member of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka, the President’s Media Division (PMD) said.

title: Health Ministry promotes dengue hotline
byline: The Health and Mass Media Ministry has called for wide public awareness of the newly established Dengue Operations Room, which has been set up to strengthen information gathering and coordination related to dengue prevention and control.

title: Sri Lanka amends National Environmental Act to strengthen environmental protection
byline: Sri Lanka has amended the National Environmental Act, introducing new legal provisions aimed at strengthening environmental protection, Deputy Minister of Environment Anton Jayakody announced at an international climate conference in Bangkok, Thailand.

title: CSE ends lower as profit-taking and cautious sentiment weigh ahead of earnings season
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange commenced the week on a weaker footing, with both benchmark indices closing lower as profit-taking in selected counters weighed on overall market performance. Selling pressure persisted throughout the session, while moderate turnover and share volume levels reflected cautious investor participation.

title: Four school students drown after boat capsizes in Wanathawilluwa lagoon
byline: Four school students have died after drowning in the Mangala Pura lagoon in Wanathawilluwa while travelling by boat to collect flowers.

title: IMF commends Sri Lanka’s progress and reaffirms support for reform programme
byline: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) delegation has commended Sri Lanka’s economic resilience and reaffirmed its support for the Government’s reform agenda during a meeting with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat this morning (30).

title: Vice Admiral Damian Fernando appointed new Navy Commander
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed Rear Admiral Damian Fernando as the new Commander of the Sri Lanka Navy. Concurrently elevated to the rank of Vice Admiral, he will take charge as the 27th Commander of the country’s naval forces.

title: Rotary car parking system introduced to Sri Lanka for the first time
byline: Sri Lanka’s first-ever rotary car parking system has been introduced, marking a significant advancement in urban parking solutions in the country.

title: Indonesia's education minister sentenced to years in jail for corruption
byline: The co-founder of super-app Gojek who became Indonesia’s education minister has been sentenced to several years in jail for corruption.

title: New priority access card for disabled persons announced
byline: The National Council for Persons with Disabilities has decided to introduce a special identification card to provide priority services for persons with disabilities at government institutions.

title: Reckless drivers to face criminal prosecution, tougher penalties: Police
byline: Sri Lanka Police have introduced tougher measures against dangerous and reckless driving, warning that serious traffic offenders will face criminal prosecution in addition to penalties under existing traffic laws.

title: Sri Lanka reaffirms climate commitment, targets 70% renewable energy by 2030
byline: Sri Lanka has reaffirmed its commitment to ambitious climate action and sustainable development goals, with plans to meet 70 per cent of the country’s energy demand through renewable sources by 2030 and beyond, Deputy Minister of Environment Anton Jayakody said.

title: Supreme Court rejects Trump bid to restrict birthright citizenship
byline: Handing President Donald Trump a stinging defeat, the U.S. Supreme Court on Tuesday rejected his audacious attempt to restrict birthright citizenship in the United States — a right long woven into the fabric of American society — scuttling one of his top priorities in his crackdown on immigration.

title: Human–elephant conflict a major national challenge: Wildlife
byline: The human–elephant conflict has become a major and challenging issue in the country, Deputy Director (Elephant Conservation) of the Department of Wildlife Conservation (DWC), U.L. Thaufeeq, said.
